implementation_notes: Added a `--in-flight` flag to `forge status` (cli/status.py). The new surface opens a short-lived read-only connection to forge.db (`read_only_connect`) and reads the `lifecycle_bridge_registry` table via `BridgeRegistry.list_active(correlation_id='cli-status:in-flight')`. New helpers: `_read_in_flight_entries`, `_build_in_flight_table`, `_serialise_in_flight_entry`, `_emit_in_flight_json`, plus the `_IN_FLIGHT_CORRELATION_ID` constant. Routing logic in `status_cmd`: when `--in-flight` is set, the command (a) rejects `--watch` and `--full` with UsageError because they are tied to the builds-table projection, (b) supports `--json` and `--db-path`, (c) accepts the positional `feature_id` as a filter, (d) falls back to the canonical line `No in-flight builds.` when the registry is empty (or the migration has never run, which is treated as empty via OperationalError-handling). The `ack_handle_token` is deliberately omitted from the JSON projection because it is internal book-keeping for the bridge's in-memory ack callback map. No imports from `forge.adapters.nats.*` were added (AC-006 import discipline preserved).

completion_promises.evidence: Added the `--in-flight` Click flag plus `_read_in_flight_entries(db_path, feature_id)` which composes `BridgeRegistry.list_active(correlation_id=_IN_FLIGHT_CORRELATION_ID)` over a `read_only_connect` handle. Verified by `TestInFlightSurface.test_in_flight_returns_registry_rows`, which seeds a registry row and asserts the rendered output contains the feature/thread/run identifiers.
